TRANSPOSED MULTIPLE-SPAN RULED SURFACE / PLANE: UNRESOLVED COMPATIBILITY BOUNDARY
Recorded: 2026-11-03
Native reference: Parasolid 38.0.150, real pskernel through PskernelSharp
API: PK_SURF_intersect_surf, default options and explicit UV areas of interest
Status: NOT a passed compatibility fixture. Public support is restricted to
        single-span transposed patches until branch semantics are resolved.

Original strict oracle result before restricting public support:
FAIL transposed-rational-ruled-four-components: transposed-rational-ruled-four-components: isolated 0/0, curves 4/2
The complete run recorded 42 passed positive fixtures and this one failure.
No branch-count gate was relaxed to turn the original failure into a pass.

Reproduction and input definition
---------------------------------
The fixture is CubicRuled(true, true, true) in
scripts/IntersectionOperationOracle.cs, intersected with the plane z=0.
The transposed multiple-span case is now replayed by TransposedRuledBoundary
outside the positive compatibility count. The untransposed multi-span and
both ordinary/rational single-span transposed fixtures remain positive cases.

Original U degree=3, V degree=1, 7 by 2 homogeneous control points.
U unique knots=[0,1,2], multiplicities=[4,3,4].
V unique knots=[0,1], multiplicities=[2,2].
For original indices i=0..6 and j=0..1:
  w_i = i % 3 + 1
  z_i = [-0.08,0.14,-0.14,0.08,-0.14,0.14,-0.08][i]
  H_ij = ((i/3)*w_i, j*w_i, z_i+j*w_i, w_i)
The original flattened offset is (i*2+j)*4. The transposed offset is
(j*7+i)*4, with U/V degrees, control counts, knots and multiplicities swapped.
Both definitions use arbitrary B-surface form, nonuniform knots, positive
weights, no periodicity, self_intersect_false and convexity_unset.

The transposed surface has U domain [0,1], V domain [0,2]. Its physical point
at (U,V)=(0.02,1.4) agrees with the untransposed surface at (1.4,0.02):
  original:   (1.4621513944223108,0.02,0.016015936254980077)
  transposed: (1.4621513944223108,0.019999999999999997,0.01601593625498007)
Thus the control-net transpose preserves the intended physical surface.

Observed native branch discrepancy
----------------------------------
Untransposed, default and full-domain hints: four bounded branches, with
nonlinear parameter intervals [0,0.2], [0.5,0.8], [1.2,1.5], [1.8,2].

Transposed, default and full-domain hints: two branches.
  Branch 0 joins V=0 to V=0.8 through an extension outside the stored U domain.
  Its native curve midpoint parameter is 0.36633833325035065, with
  XYZ=(0.3545147482795628,-0.0047435210856708356,-9.107298248878237E-18)
  and UV=(-0.004743521085670838,0.2662212866631635). U is negative.
  Branch 1 covers V=[1.8,2]. The bounded V=[1.2,1.5] component is absent.

Transposed, second-span UV area of interest U=[0,1], V=[1,2]: two branches,
now covering V=[1.8,2] and V=[1.2,1.5]. The previously absent bounded branch
has endpoints at V=1.2 and V=1.5 on U=0.

The documented API treats UV boxes as areas of interest and permits extensions.
These observations establish an unresolved orientation/hint-dependent native
branch-selection difference; they do not establish a general replacement
contract. The implementation does not discard valid bounded branches or join
them through an out-of-domain extension merely to match this one count.

Resulting public boundary
------------------------
Linear V / nonlinear U retains multiple-span support. Linear U / nonlinear V
retains verified single-span support. More than one nonempty nonlinear V span
returns PK_ERROR_not_implemented before producing any branch. Tests cover both
surface argument orders, ordinary and rational inputs, cleared return buffers,
unchanged live-curve counts and unchanged return-buffer allocation counts.
